name: R15 AREA-eligible institution (undergraduate-focused)
what: An institutional standing that opens the [R15 AREA](#term:r15) programme. It describes an accredited public or non-profit private school that [grants](#term:grant) baccalaureate degrees in biomedical sciences, enrols more undergraduates than graduate students, and has had limited [NIH](#term:nih) support [7](#cite:7).
who_qualifies: The undergraduate enrolment is greater than the graduate enrolment, and the institution has not received NIH support totaling more than $6 million per year, in direct and [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) together, in 4 of the last 7 years; health professional schools are excluded from AREA [7](#cite:7).
how_decided: The institution certifies it: a signed letter from the provost or similar official verifying eligibility goes in the application; for a multi-campus institution each campus with its own [UEI](#term:uei) or IPF number is assessed separately [45](#cite:45) [7](#cite:7).

name: R15 REAP-eligible institution (health professional school or graduate school)
what: An institutional standing that opens the [R15 REAP](#term:r15) programme. It describes an accredited public or non-profit private school that [grants](#term:grant) baccalaureate or advanced degrees in health professions or biomedical and behavioral sciences and has had limited [NIH](#term:nih) support [8](#cite:8).
who_qualifies: All components of the institution combined have not received NIH support totaling more than $6 million per year, in direct and [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) together, in 4 of the last 7 years; health professional schools are those granting degrees such as BSN, MD, DDS, PharmD, DVM and MPH, and graduate schools grant M.A., M.S. and Ph.D. degrees [8](#cite:8).
how_decided: The institution certifies it with a signed letter from the provost or similar official [45](#cite:45).

name: NIH Early Stage Investigator (ESI)
what: An investigator standing. An [Early Stage Investigator](#term:early-stage-investigator) is a [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) within 10 years of the terminal research degree or the end of post-graduate clinical training, whichever is later, who has not yet won a substantial independent [NIH](#term:nih) research award [138](#cite:138).
who_qualifies: The status applies to R01-equivalent applications, and every PD/PI on the application must hold it for the application to be treated as an ESI application [138](#cite:138).
how_decided: NIH computes the status from the degree date and award history in the investigator's [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons) profile, and considers extensions for lapses in research or training [138](#cite:138).

name: Nonprofit other than an institution of higher education (with or without 501(c)(3) status)
what: The eligibility class [NIH](#term:nih) notices use for non-profits that are not universities. It appears as two lines in the eligibility section of a notice: nonprofits with [501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) IRS status and nonprofits without it, in both cases other than [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) [4](#cite:4).
who_qualifies: Both lines are eligible in the parent [R01](#term:r01), [R21](#term:r21-r03), R03 and R13 notices, the MIRA notices, the NIAID P01 and [U01](#term:u01) notices read, and the four NIH Director's award notices; neither is eligible for the [R15](#term:r15), which is limited to institutions of higher education [4](#cite:4) [5](#cite:5) [6](#cite:6) [52](#cite:52) [73](#cite:73) [113](#cite:113) [116](#cite:116) [75](#cite:75) [7](#cite:7).
how_decided: Each [notice of funding opportunity](#term:nofo) lists its own eligible organization types [4](#cite:4).

pending_changes.text: [NIH](#term:nih) no longer issues awards that include a [subaward](#term:subaward) to a foreign entity; direct awards to foreign organizations continue, and paid foreign collaborators on a U.S.-led project are funded through linked awards under the PF5 structure [22](#cite:22) [86](#cite:86).

name: Foreign (non-U.S.) organization
what: The eligibility class for organizations outside the United States. The [Grants](#term:grant) Policy Statement says foreign and international organizations may apply for research project grants and may not apply for programme project, center, institutional training, resource, SBIR/STTR or construction grants [107](#cite:107).
who_qualifies: Foreign organizations are eligible for the parent [R01](#term:r01), [R21 and R03](#term:r21-r03) and for some institute notices such as NIAID's clinical trial [U01](#term:u01); they are not eligible for the [R15](#term:r15), the R13, MIRA, the NIAID P01 or the NIH Director's awards [4](#cite:4) [5](#cite:5) [6](#cite:6) [116](#cite:116) [7](#cite:7) [52](#cite:52) [73](#cite:73) [113](#cite:113) [75](#cite:75).
how_decided: Each notice states whether non-domestic entities may apply; a foreign applicant uses a detailed budget and receives [F&A](#term:indirect-costs) at 8 percent of [modified total direct costs](#term:mtdc) [36](#cite:36) [64](#cite:64).

pending_changes.text: [NSF](#term:nsf) has proposed to replace the [PAPPG](#term:pappg) with a Guidance on [Financial Assistance](#term:financial-assistance); comments closed August 24, 2026 and NSF's stated goal is to issue it for use in early to mid FY2027 [152](#cite:152) [151](#cite:151).

name: Institution of higher education eligible for NSF funding
what: Two- and four-year [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education), community colleges included, accredited in and with a campus located in the U.S. [156](#cite:156).
who_qualifies: Accreditation in the U.S. and a U.S. campus; an institution outside the U.S. is treated as a foreign organisation, which NSF rarely funds directly [156](#cite:156). Since December 8, 2025 an institution that maintains a contract or agreement with a Confucius Institute may not receive NSF funds without a waiver from the NSF Director [149](#cite:149).
how_decided: Set by the PAPPG, Chapter I.E [156](#cite:156).

pending_changes.text: [NSF](#term:nsf) has proposed to replace the [PAPPG](#term:pappg) with a Guidance on [Financial Assistance](#term:financial-assistance); comments closed August 24, 2026 and NSF's stated goal is to issue it for use in early to mid FY2027 [152](#cite:152) [151](#cite:151).

name: Non-profit, non-academic organisation (NSF proposer category)
what: NSF's category for independent museums, observatories, research laboratories, professional societies and similar organisations located in the U.S. that are directly associated with educational or research activities [156](#cite:156).
who_qualifies: The test is the organisation's direct association with educational or research activities and a U.S. location; the PAPPG text read does not mention tax status [156](#cite:156). NSF's getting-started page lists nonprofit organisations beside universities and tribal nations as eligible [158](#cite:158).
how_decided: Set by the PAPPG, Chapter I.E; a [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) may narrow it, as Expeditions in Computing and RUI do [156](#cite:156) [191](#cite:191) [254](#cite:254).

name: Tribal Nation (Indian Tribe) as NSF proposer
what: A federally recognised American Indian or Alaska Native tribe, band, nation, pueblo, village or community is an eligible [NSF](#term:nsf) proposer [156](#cite:156).
who_qualifies: Tribes acknowledged by the Secretary of the Interior as federally recognised [156](#cite:156). Supplement 1 changed the [PAPPG](#term:pappg) term from Tribal Nations to Indian Tribes [149](#cite:149).
how_decided: Set by the PAPPG, Chapter I.E, by reference to federal recognition [156](#cite:156).

name: Predominantly undergraduate institution (PUI) for RUI and ROA
what: An accredited college or university, two-year community colleges included, that awards associate's, bachelor's or master's degrees in NSF-supported fields and few doctorates [254](#cite:254).
who_qualifies: Institutions that have awarded 20 or fewer Ph.D./D.Sci. degrees in all NSF-supported fields during the combined previous two academic years [254](#cite:254).
how_decided: By the institution's own certification: an RUI proposal carries a Certification of RUI/ROA Eligibility [254](#cite:254).

name: U.S. institution of higher education with degree-granting programmes in science or engineering (MURI)
what: The class of institution that may receive MURI funds [325](#cite:325).
who_qualifies: U.S. [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) with degree-granting programmes in science and/or engineering; industry, department laboratories, FFRDCs and foreign entities may collaborate but may not receive MURI funds [325](#cite:325).
how_decided: Set in the yearly MURI announcement [325](#cite:325).

name: Extramural organisation (CDMRP)
what: [CDMRP](#term:cdmrp) sorts applicants into extramural organisations, which are outside the department, and intramural ones, which are inside it; the two submit by different routes [330](#cite:330).
who_qualifies: An eligible organisation outside the department; CDMRP's general instructions give academia, biotechnology companies, foundations, government and research institutes as examples [359](#cite:359). FY26 announcements include foreign and domestic, for-profit and non-profit organisations [330](#cite:330).
how_decided: Defined in CDMRP's general application instructions and in each programme announcement [359](#cite:359) [330](#cite:330).

name: Non-profit other than a section 501(c)(4) organisation that lobbies (DOE)
what: DOE notices read in this sweep admit non-profit organisations but exclude one class of them [278](#cite:278) [301](#cite:301).
who_qualifies: In the [Office of Science](#term:doe-office-of-science) FY 2027 notice, non-profits described in section 501(c)(4) that engaged in lobbying activities after December 31, 1995 are ineligible [278](#cite:278). The ARPA-E example notice states that non-profits described in section 501(c)(4) are not eligible applicants [301](#cite:301).
how_decided: Set in each DOE notice [278](#cite:278) [301](#cite:301).

name: AFRI strengthening (FASE) eligible institution
what: Institutions that qualify for [AFRI](#term:nifa)'s Food and Agricultural Science Enhancement (FASE) strengthening [grants](#term:grant): seed, equipment, sabbatical and strengthening standard or coordinated project grants paid from reserved funds [423](#cite:423).
who_qualifies: Small and mid-sized institutions (total enrolment of 17,500 or less), [minority-serving institutions](#term:minority-serving-institution) (one or more minority groups exceed 50 percent of enrolment), and institutions in the FY 2026 [EPSCoR](#term:epscor) states: Alaska, Connecticut, Delaware, Hawaii, Idaho, Kentucky, Maine, Montana, North Dakota, New Jersey, New Mexico, Nevada, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Utah, Vermont, West Virginia and Wyoming, plus listed territories and the District of Columbia. The funding thresholds that also apply were not returned by the fetch [423](#cite:423).
how_decided: By NIFA's published definitions and its yearly list of states; NIFA publishes a flow chart for strengthening eligibility [423](#cite:423) [420](#cite:420).

name: AFRI new investigator
what: An early-career [project director](#term:principal-investigator) who may apply for [AFRI](#term:nifa) [new investigator](#term:early-stage-investigator) [grants](#term:grant) [423](#cite:423).
who_qualifies: Fewer than 75 total publications, fewer than 25 as first or senior author, and less than five years of postgraduate career-track experience, not more than 12 years beyond the terminal degree [423](#cite:423).
how_decided: By NIFA's definition; NIFA publishes a decision tree [423](#cite:423) [420](#cite:420).

name: Institution eligible for AFRI integrated projects
what: [AFRI](#term:nifa) integrated projects (research combined with education or extension) have a narrower applicant list than single-function projects [474](#cite:474) [412](#cite:412).
who_qualifies: Colleges and universities, 1994 [land-grant institutions](#term:land-grant-institution), and Hispanic-serving agricultural colleges and universities; a research foundation maintained by a college or university is eligible. Other non-profits and private organizations are not on the list [412](#cite:412) [474](#cite:474).
how_decided: Stated in each AFRI notice [412](#cite:412).

name: State Water Resources Research Institute
what: One of the 54 institutes or centres established under the Water Resources Research Act, one in each state and in the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands and Guam. Only the institutes may submit applications under the Act's [grant](#term:grant) programmes [483](#cite:483) [486](#cite:486).
who_qualifies: The institute itself is the applicant; investigators at accredited institutions of higher learning apply through it [485](#cite:485).
how_decided: Set by the Water Resources Research Act of 1984 [486](#cite:486).

name: Sea Grant programme
what: One of the 34 Sea [Grant](#term:grant) programmes. Many National Sea Grant Office notices take applications only from these programmes, and each programme runs its own opportunities for researchers [437](#cite:437) [436](#cite:436).
who_qualifies: The 34 Sea Grant programmes listed by the National Sea Grant Office [437](#cite:437).
how_decided: By designation within the National Sea Grant College Program; the designation process was not on the pages read [437](#cite:437).

name: University Transportation Center consortium led by a non-profit institution of higher education
what: A University Transportation Center must be a consortium of two or more non-profit [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) led by one lead institution, all in the United States, its territories or on Tribal lands [493](#cite:493).
who_qualifies: Only US non-profit institutions of higher education as defined under 20 U.S.C. 1001(a) may apply, and an institution may receive one [grant](#term:grant) as lead through a competition [493](#cite:493).
how_decided: Set by statute, 49 U.S.C. 5505(b) [493](#cite:493).

name: Minority entity or Indian tribe (NIDILRR Field Initiated Projects, MSI competition)
what: The class of applicant to which [NIDILRR](#term:acl) limits its [minority-serving institution](#term:minority-serving-institution) competitions for Field Initiated Projects [579](#cite:579).
who_qualifies: A historically black college or university, a [Hispanic-serving institution](#term:hispanic-serving-institution), an American Indian [tribal college](#term:tribal-college) or university, another institution where minority student enrollment is at least 50 percent, or an Indian tribe [579](#cite:579).
how_decided: Defined in the [notice of funding opportunity](#term:nofo), which cites 29 U.S.C. 718 among its authorities [579](#cite:579).

name: VA-paid appointment of at least 5/8ths time
what: The employment standing an investigator needs to submit for intramural VA research funding. It attaches to the person, through a VA medical centre, and not to an outside institution [584](#cite:584) [583](#cite:583).
who_qualifies: A [principal investigator](#term:principal-investigator) with at least 5/8ths VA-paid effort, or who is brought to 5/8ths by accepting the funds; non-clinicians may need to meet additional eligibility requirements [583](#cite:583).
how_decided: Set by VA; a joint university and VA appointment needs a memorandum of understanding stating the appointment, pay distribution and effort at each institution [584](#cite:584).

name: NEH eligible organisation
what: The class of applicants that the 2026 [NEH](#term:neh) notices for organisations accept [632](#cite:632) [634](#cite:634) [648](#cite:648).
who_qualifies: Nonprofit organizations recognized as tax-exempt under [section 501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3); accredited [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education), public or nonprofit; state and local governments and their agencies; federally recognized Native American Tribal governments [632](#cite:632) [648](#cite:648). Individuals and foreign and for-profit entities are ineligible [632](#cite:632) [648](#cite:648).
how_decided: Stated in each [Notice of Funding Opportunity](#term:nofo); NEH staff screen applications for eligibility [648](#cite:648).

name: NEA five-year history of operations
what: A threshold in the [NEA](#term:nea) research award guidelines: the [applicant organisation](#term:applicant-organization) must have operated for five years before the deadline [651](#cite:651).
who_qualifies: For Research [Grants](#term:grant) in the Arts, a [501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) nonprofit, unit of state or local government, or federally recognized tribe with a five-year history of operations prior to the application deadline [651](#cite:651). For Research Labs, a U.S. [institution of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) or 501(c)(3) nonprofit whose five-year history includes commissioning and conducting research [652](#cite:652).
how_decided: Set in the programme guidelines and checked by NEA staff for eligibility [652](#cite:652).

name: IMLS eligible library or archives entity
what: The three-part eligibility test in the FY 2027 National Leadership [Grants](#term:grant) for Libraries notice [677](#cite:677).
who_qualifies: An organisation that is (1) a unit of State, local or Tribal government or a private nonprofit with [501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) status, (2) located in one of the 50 states, the District of Columbia or a listed territory or freely associated state, and (3) a library or its parent organisation, an academic or administrative unit such as a graduate school of library and information science, a digital library or archives, a library or archival agency, a consortium, an association, or a nonprofit whose sole mission is to support an affiliated library or archives [677](#cite:677). A library must be open and operational to the public when the application is submitted [677](#cite:677).
how_decided: Stated in the notice; [IMLS](#term:imls) generally rejects applications from institutions it determines to be ineligible [677](#cite:677).

name: IMLS eligible museum or related entity
what: The eligibility test in the FY 2027 National Leadership [Grants](#term:grant) for Museums notice [681](#cite:681).
who_qualifies: A unit of State, local or Tribal government or a private nonprofit organization that is a museum using a professional staff and organised on a permanent basis for essentially educational, cultural heritage or aesthetic purposes; the notice also lists [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education), including public and nonprofit universities [681](#cite:681). The full list of other eligible entity types was not captured [681](#cite:681).
how_decided: Stated in the notice [681](#cite:681).

name: IES applicant with the ability and capacity to conduct rigorous research
what: The eligibility sentence [IES](#term:ies) uses across its research competitions; it does not restrict applicants by type of organisation [663](#cite:663) [662](#cite:662).
who_qualifies: Institutions that have the ability and capacity to conduct rigorous research, including non-profit and for-profit organizations and public and private agencies and institutions such as colleges and universities [663](#cite:663) [716](#cite:716).
how_decided: Stated in each request for applications and in the [Federal Register](#term:federal-register) notice [662](#cite:662).

name: NRSA citizenship and residency requirement
what: To hold a Kirschstein-NRSA fellowship or a trainee place on an [NRSA](#term:nrsa) [training grant](#term:t32), a person must be a citizen or a non-citizen national of the United States, or lawfully admitted for permanent residence [736](#cite:736) [750](#cite:750). The notices name no other status [741](#cite:741). The mentored [K awards](#term:k-award) read in this sweep use the same wording, while the K99 has no citizenship requirement [744](#cite:744) [743](#cite:743).
who_qualifies: U.S. citizens, non-citizen nationals and lawful permanent residents; a permanent resident holds a currently valid Permanent Resident Card (USCIS Form I-551) or other legal verification of status [741](#cite:741).
how_decided: Set in each notice. For fellowships the status must be held by the time of award; for training grants, at the time of appointment [736](#cite:736) [750](#cite:750). A June 2025 correction fixed the wording of the five parent fellowship notices to read 'non-citizen national' [757](#cite:757).

pending_changes.text: The K99 code is to be replaced by KT1/R00 for due dates on or after October 12, 2027; the pages read do not say whether the 4-year window changes [742](#cite:742) [758](#cite:758).

name: K99/R00 eligibility window (no more than 4 years of postdoctoral research experience)
what: A [K99/R00](#term:k-award) candidate must have no more than 4 years of postdoctoral research experience on the application due date [743](#cite:743). There is no citizenship requirement, and the notice says a candidate may be a non-U.S. citizen [743](#cite:743).
who_qualifies: Holders of a clinical or research doctorate with no more than 4 years of postdoctoral research experience; [NIH](#term:nih) approves a one-year extension for childbirth, and parental, medical or military leave is typically not counted [743](#cite:743).
how_decided: Counted against the due date of the application; set in the notice [743](#cite:743). NIH issued automatic extensions in June 2025 and January 2026 for windows that closed during delays in 2025 and early 2026 [791](#cite:791) [790](#cite:790).

name: Domestic organization (required for NIH career, training and research education awards)
what: The parent K, K12, [T32](#term:t32), T35, R25 and F99/K00 notices read in this sweep are open only to domestic organizations: foreign organizations and non-domestic components of U.S. organizations may not apply [744](#cite:744) [753](#cite:753) [750](#cite:750) [751](#cite:751) [756](#cite:756) [741](#cite:741). The [NRSA](#term:nrsa) fellowships [F31](#term:f-award), F32 and F33 differ: foreign organizations are on their eligible lists [736](#cite:736) [737](#cite:737) [739](#cite:739). Within the domestic group, non-profits other than [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education), with or without [501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) status, are listed as eligible in every one of these notices [744](#cite:744) [750](#cite:750) [753](#cite:753) [756](#cite:756).
who_qualifies: U.S. higher education institutions, non-profits with or without 501(c)(3) status, and the other domestic organization types each notice lists [744](#cite:744) [750](#cite:750).
how_decided: Set in Section III of each notice [744](#cite:744).

name: Researcher eligible for NIH extramural loan repayment
what: A researcher qualifies for the Extramural [Loan Repayment Program](#term:loan-repayment) by meeting tests of degree, citizenship, research time, debt and employer, not by holding an [NIH](#term:nih) [grant](#term:grant) [762](#cite:762).
who_qualifies: A holder of a doctoral-level health or research degree who is a U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident, does qualified research at least 20 hours a week, has educational debt of at least 20 percent of institutional base salary, and whose research is supported by a domestic non-profit institution or a U.S. government agency [762](#cite:762). Federal employees working more than 20 hours a week and employees of for-profit institutions are excluded [763](#cite:763).
how_decided: The applicant states the facts and an Institutional Business Official certifies them [763](#cite:763).

name: Institution eligible for the NIGMS BURT undergraduate training programme
what: BURT is limited to organizations that enroll undergraduates and have had modest [NIH](#term:nih) research funding [797](#cite:797).
who_qualifies: An organization that enrolls undergraduates and has received NIH Research Project [Grant](#term:grant) funding averaging less than $50 million in total costs (direct and indirect) a year over the last three fiscal years [797](#cite:797).
how_decided: By the funding test written into the notice [797](#cite:797).

name: Institution with or without an NIH-funded dual-degree training programme (F30 split)
what: Which [F30](#term:f-award) notice a student uses depends on the institution: one [parent notice](#term:parent-announcement) is limited to [applicant organizations](#term:applicant-organization) with an NIH-funded institutional predoctoral dual-degree training programme, such as a Medical Scientist Training Program or Dental Scientist Training Program, and the other to organizations without one [784](#cite:784) [738](#cite:738).
who_qualifies: Organizations with such a programme use PA-25-426; organizations without one use PA-25-425 [784](#cite:784) [738](#cite:738).
how_decided: By whether the organization holds an NIH-funded dual-degree [training grant](#term:t32); some institutes fund only one side, for example NIBIB and NINDS do not fund F30 applications from institutions that hold such programmes [804](#cite:804).

name: CAREER-eligible principal investigator
what: The set of conditions a person must meet to be the investigator on a CAREER proposal [815](#cite:815).
who_qualifies: A person who holds a doctoral degree in a field [NSF](#term:nsf) supports, holds at least a 50% tenure-track or tenure-track-equivalent position as an assistant professor or equivalent, is untenured, has not received a [CAREER award](#term:nsf-career), and has taken part in fewer than three CAREER competitions [815](#cite:815). A tenure-track-equivalent post is a continuing appointment expected to last the five years of the [grant](#term:grant), with substantial research and educational duties, where the project fits the person's job and the organisation's mission [815](#cite:815). Associate professors are not eligible, with or without tenure [816](#cite:816).
how_decided: The department head's letter in the proposal confirms eligibility; the rules are set by the [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) [815](#cite:815).

pending_changes.text: The FY 2025 [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) let a graduate student apply who had completed no more than one academic year; the FY 2026 solicitation limited the graduate category to first-year students with less than one academic year completed; the FY 2027 solicitation adds that second-year graduate students are not eligible [885](#cite:885) [859](#cite:859) [818](#cite:818).

name: GRFP-eligible applicant
what: The academic levels, citizenship and field rules a person must meet to apply for a Graduate Research Fellowship in the FY 2027 competition [818](#cite:818).
who_qualifies: A U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident who is a final-year undergraduate, a bachelor's degree holder never enrolled in a graduate degree programme, a joint bachelor's-master's student in the final undergraduate or first graduate year, or a first-year graduate student in a first graduate programme with less than one academic year completed [818](#cite:818) [820](#cite:820). Second-year graduate students do not qualify [818](#cite:818). The degree sought must be a research-based master's or doctorate in an eligible STEM field, not a professional or practice-oriented degree [818](#cite:818) [820](#cite:820).
how_decided: Set each year by the solicitation; [NSF](#term:nsf) checks academic status against the registrar's transcript at the application deadline and may return an application without review if the applicant, degree programme, field or proposed research is ineligible [818](#cite:818) [861](#cite:861).

name: NSF postdoctoral fellowship applicant
what: [NSF](#term:nsf) does not fund unaffiliated individuals, with one stated exception: a person who submits to an NSF postdoctoral fellowship [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) is not treated as unaffiliated [156](#cite:156).
who_qualifies: Each fellowship solicitation sets its own career window [837](#cite:837) [840](#cite:840) [842](#cite:842) [880](#cite:880). All those read require U.S. citizenship, nationality or permanent residence [837](#cite:837) [840](#cite:840) [842](#cite:842) [880](#cite:880) [833](#cite:833). Biology allows no more than 15 full-time months in posts requiring a doctorate; mathematical sciences allows the doctorate to have been held no more than two years; astronomy allows five years since the doctorate; atmospheric and geospace sciences allows a PhD held for no more than two years or less than 18 months of full-time employment [837](#cite:837) [840](#cite:840) [842](#cite:842) [880](#cite:880).
how_decided: Set by each fellowship solicitation [837](#cite:837) [840](#cite:840) [842](#cite:842).

name: Institution not classified R1 (NSF research-initiation and traineeship rules)
what: Several [NSF](#term:nsf) career-stage and training programmes are open only to institutions that the Carnegie Classification does not place among Doctoral Universities with Very High Research Activity ([R1](#term:r1-institution)) [832](#cite:832) [828](#cite:828).
who_qualifies: An [institution of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) not currently classified R1 [832](#cite:832). The rule opens Engineering Research Initiation and Track 2 of the Research Traineeship [832](#cite:832) [828](#cite:828). The archived CRII, LEAPS-MPS and BRC-BIO programmes used similar tests [843](#cite:843) [844](#cite:844) [845](#cite:845).
how_decided: By the institution's Carnegie Classification, as each [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) states [832](#cite:832) [828](#cite:828).

pending_changes.text: The eligibility freeze runs through FY 2027; what applies after that was not stated on the page read [878](#cite:878).

name: NSF EPSCoR jurisdiction
what: [EPSCoR](#term:epscor) is [NSF](#term:nsf)'s programme to raise the research competitiveness of targeted jurisdictions, each a state, territory or commonwealth [866](#cite:866). An institution's location in an eligible jurisdiction decides whether it can apply to the EPSCoR Graduate Fellowship Program and EPSCoR Research Fellows [825](#cite:825) [867](#cite:867).
who_qualifies: An institution with a campus in an eligible EPSCoR jurisdiction at the time of submission [825](#cite:825). NSF lists 28 eligible jurisdictions: Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Delaware, Guam, Hawaii, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Vermont, U.S. Virgin Islands, West Virginia and Wyoming [878](#cite:878) [877](#cite:877).
how_decided: NSF's eligibility page says the CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 in effect freezes jurisdiction eligibility through FY 2027, and that no new jurisdictions will be considered eligible through FY 2027 [878](#cite:878). The percentage rule behind the list was not in the text returned [878](#cite:878).

name: Investigator eligible for the DOE Office of Science Early Career Research Program
what: The career-stage rule that decides who may lead an Early Career Research Program application [890](#cite:890).
who_qualifies: An untenured, tenure-track assistant or associate professor at a U.S. academic institution, or a full-time employee at a DOE national laboratory or [Office of Science](#term:doe-office-of-science) user facility, within 10 years of the doctorate [890](#cite:890).
how_decided: Set by the programme and stated in each year's notice; the FY 2026 notice was not read [890](#cite:890) [909](#cite:909).

name: Institution whose faculty may apply to the DOE Visiting Faculty Program
what: The institution test for the Visiting Faculty Program: it turns on the Carnegie research classification of the college or university where the faculty member teaches [902](#cite:902).
who_qualifies: An institution that is not classed Research 1 or Research 2 in the 2025 Carnegie Classification; faculty at Historically Black Colleges and Universities qualify whatever the classification [902](#cite:902).
how_decided: By the 2025 Carnegie Classification, as the programme's eligibility page applies it [902](#cite:902).

name: Institution eligible for NIFA National Needs Fellowship grants
what: The kind of institution that may apply for a National Needs Graduate and Postgraduate Fellowship [grant](#term:grant) [962](#cite:962).
who_qualifies: [Land-grant institutions](#term:land-grant-institution) and other colleges and universities with a demonstrable capacity to carry out the teaching of food and agricultural sciences, which confer graduate degrees [962](#cite:962). The opportunity page also lists [Hispanic-serving institutions](#term:hispanic-serving-institution), colleges with significant minority enrolments and research foundations maintained by eligible institutions [961](#cite:961).
how_decided: Stated in the [notice of funding opportunity](#term:nofo) [962](#cite:962).

name: Individual eligible for NEH awards to individuals
what: [NEH](#term:neh)'s fellowship-type awards are made to people, not organisations, and one notice sets who counts as an eligible person [987](#cite:987).
who_qualifies: A U.S. citizen living in the United States or abroad, or a foreign national who has lived in the United States or its jurisdictions for at least the three years before the deadline; not currently enrolled in a degree-granting programme; no institutional affiliation needed [987](#cite:987).
how_decided: Set by the NEH [notice of funding opportunity](#term:nofo) for awards to individuals, amended April 1, 2026 [987](#cite:987).

name: IES early career researcher
what: The condition a [principal investigator](#term:principal-investigator) must meet for an [IES](#term:ies) Early Career Development and Mentoring award [995](#cite:995) [997](#cite:997).
who_qualifies: For FY 2027: a doctorate completed no earlier than April 1, 2019 and no later than the start of the award; a faculty or research scientist post; no tenure at the application deadline for faculty; U.S. citizen or permanent resident; never principal or [co-principal investigator](#term:multiple-pi) on an IES [grant](#term:grant) [995](#cite:995) [997](#cite:997).
how_decided: Set in each year's request for applications; citizenship and prior IES roles are checked if the application is recommended for funding [995](#cite:995).

name: Institution with earlier HRSA funding under Public Health Service Act sections 736, 739 or 747
what: The FY 2026 [HRSA](#term:hrsa) primary care [National Research Service Award](#term:nrsa) is open only to [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) that already held certain HRSA training awards [1028](#cite:1028).
who_qualifies: A domestic public or private nonprofit institution of higher education that received funding between 2011 and 2025 under section 736, 739 or 747 of the Public Health Service Act [1028](#cite:1028).
how_decided: Stated in the [notice of funding opportunity](#term:nofo) [1028](#cite:1028).

name: Nationally representative behavioral health professional organization (SAMHSA Minority Fellowship Program)
what: The class of organisation that could apply for a Minority Fellowship Program [grant](#term:grant) in the FY 2024 notice [1037](#cite:1037).
who_qualifies: Nationally representative mental health or substance use disorder treatment professional organizations in psychiatry, nursing, social work, psychology, marriage and family therapy, mental health counseling, substance use disorder and addictions counseling, or addiction medicine [1037](#cite:1037).
how_decided: Stated in the [notice of funding opportunity](#term:nofo) [1037](#cite:1037).

name: Independent research institution (NEH Fellowship Programs at Independent Research Institutions)
what: The class of organisation that could apply for [NEH](#term:neh)'s [grant](#term:grant) to run its own humanities fellowships - a research body that is not a university [1047](#cite:1047) [1050](#cite:1050).
who_qualifies: Independent centers for advanced study, libraries and museums in the United States, American overseas research centers, and American organizations that promote humanities research abroad [1047](#cite:1047). The 2021 and 2022 terms required [501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) status and excluded [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education); a centre affiliated with a university qualified only if financed, governed and administered independently [1050](#cite:1050). The 2023 listing also names state, local and tribal governments as applicant types [1049](#cite:1049).
how_decided: Set by NEH in each [notice of funding opportunity](#term:nofo); the 2023 and 2024 notice itself could not be read [1049](#cite:1049).

name: Health Center Program look-alike designation
what: A look-alike is an organization that meets all Health Center Program requirements and receives no programme [grant](#term:grant). Designation brings Federally Qualified Health Center payment for Medicare and Medicaid patients, 340B drug discounts, Vaccines for Children and access to National Health Service Corps providers. Federal Tort Claims Act malpractice coverage does not extend to look-alikes [1155](#cite:1155).
who_qualifies: A public or nonprofit entity that serves areas or populations lacking access to primary care; the full criteria are in the Bureau's application instructions [1216](#cite:1216).
how_decided: By application to [HRSA](#term:hrsa) through the [Electronic Handbooks](#term:hrsa-ehbs) at any time; the applicant has 90 days to complete the application. Designated organizations then file an annual certification and a [renewal](#term:renewal) [1216](#cite:1216) [1155](#cite:1155).

name: Recovery Community Organization (RCO)
what: The class of organization to which Building Communities of Recovery [grants](#term:grant) are limited by statute [1118](#cite:1118).
who_qualifies: An independent nonprofit organization that mobilizes resources to increase the prevalence and quality of long-term recovery from substance use disorders and is wholly or principally governed by people in recovery who reflect the community served [1117](#cite:1117) [1206](#cite:1206).
how_decided: Set by the programme's statute, as the notice states; the applicant shows in its application that it meets the definition [1118](#cite:1118).

name: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline network crisis centre
what: A crisis centre that is part of the 988 Lifeline network and provides 24/7 services. Only such centres could apply for the FY 2026 crisis centre follow-up notice [1122](#cite:1122).
who_qualifies: Crisis centers that are part of the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline Network and provide 24/7 services [1122](#cite:1122).
how_decided: By membership of the Lifeline network; no page read describes how a centre joins [1122](#cite:1122).

name: HUD-approved housing counselling agency
what: An agency approved to take part in HUD's Housing Counseling Program. Approval must be in place before the [grant](#term:grant) notice is issued [1290](#cite:1290).
who_qualifies: Agencies HUD has approved for its Housing Counseling Program; state housing finance agencies qualify where they have statutory authority for statewide counselling; the [forecast](#term:forecast) does not give the approval criteria [1290](#cite:1290).
how_decided: By HUD approval, before the notice issue date [1290](#cite:1290).

name: Eligible agency for a centre for independent living
what: The kind of organisation that may hold a Part C centre for independent living [grant](#term:grant): consumer-controlled, community-based, cross-disability, non-residential and a private non-profit [1258](#cite:1258).
who_qualifies: A private non-profit agency that meets all five terms and can carry out the functions in section 725(b) and (c) of the Rehabilitation Act [1258](#cite:1258). [ACL](#term:acl) reports that people with disabilities hold 75 percent of decision-making positions in centres [1262](#cite:1262).
how_decided: Defined by the Rehabilitation Act and applied in each competition notice [1258](#cite:1258).

name: Non-profit eligible as a Nonprofit Security Grant Program subapplicant
what: The class of organisation that may be a subapplicant under NSGP: described under [section 501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) of the Internal Revenue Code and exempt from tax under section 501(a) [1320](#cite:1320).
who_qualifies: A 501(c)(3) organisation; churches, mosques and synagogues qualify without an IRS recognition of exemption [1320](#cite:1320).
how_decided: By the Internal Revenue Code definition, checked by the [State Administrative Agency](#term:state-administering-agency) and FEMA reviewers [1320](#cite:1320).

name: Existing LSC grantee
what: An organisation that already holds an [LSC](#term:legal-services-corporation) [grant](#term:grant). LSC's technology, pro bono, disaster and veterans appeals grants are open only to this class [1323](#cite:1323).
who_qualifies: The 129 legal aid programmes LSC funds through Basic Field Grants [1328](#cite:1328).
how_decided: By holding a current LSC grant [1323](#cite:1323).

name: Designated Head Start agency
what: An agency designated to run Head Start in a service area for five years. At the end of the period it is renewed without competition unless it meets one of seven conditions, in which case the area is opened to other applicants [1226](#cite:1226).
who_qualifies: A local public or private non-profit organisation, including a faith-based organisation, or a local for-profit organisation, selected for the service area [1229](#cite:1229).
how_decided: By [ACF](#term:acf) under 45 [CFR](#term:cfr) part 1304, subpart B [1226](#cite:1226).

name: Certified Community Development Financial Institution (and emerging CDFI)
what: Certification by the [CDFI](#term:cdfi) Fund is the gate to its [Financial Assistance](#term:financial-assistance) awards: each applicant for those must be a certified CDFI [1434](#cite:1434). An emerging CDFI, one that can show it will be certified within three years, may apply for Technical Assistance [1433](#cite:1433).
who_qualifies: An organisation the CDFI Fund has certified [1434](#cite:1434). The certification application's information collection was put out for comment on September 30, 2026 [1436](#cite:1436).
how_decided: By the CDFI Fund, on application [1436](#cite:1436).

name: ARC county economic status
what: ARC classes each Appalachian county as distressed, at-risk, transitional, competitive or attainment, and the class sets how much of a project ARC may pay [1446](#cite:1446).
who_qualifies: A project is classed by the county or counties it serves: up to 80 percent ARC funding for distressed, 70 for at-risk, 50 for transitional and 30 for competitive counties; attainment counties are generally ineligible [1446](#cite:1446).
how_decided: By ARC's designation of each county; the method and the fiscal year of the current designations were not read [1446](#cite:1446).

name: EDA economic distress criteria
what: EDA's Public Works and Economic Adjustment [grants](#term:grant) are limited to projects in regions that meet a distress test, and the level of distress sets the largest share EDA may pay [1432](#cite:1432).
who_qualifies: A region with an unemployment rate at least one percentage point above the national average, or per capita income at 80 percent or less of the national average, or a special need as EDA determines [1432](#cite:1432).
how_decided: By regulation, 13 [CFR](#term:cfr) 301.3 and 301.4, applied by EDA to the data in the application [1432](#cite:1432).

name: NIH IDeA-eligible state
what: An institution is [IDeA-eligible](#term:idea-program) by its location: it must be in one of the states [NIH](#term:nih) lists as IDeA-eligible [1546](#cite:1546). The IDeA programme was authorised by Congress in 1993 to build biomedical research capacity in states with historically low NIH [grant](#term:grant) funding [success rates](#term:success-rate) [1545](#cite:1545).
who_qualifies: Institutions in Alaska, Arkansas, Delaware, Hawaii, Idaho, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Vermont, West Virginia, Wyoming and Puerto Rico, as listed on the NIGMS page last updated December 10, 2025 [1543](#cite:1543) and in the notices posted in June and August 2026 [1546](#cite:1546) [1545](#cite:1545). The list is 23 states and Puerto Rico [1584](#cite:1584).
how_decided: NIH publishes the list; the pages and notices fetched do not state the rule or threshold by which a state enters or leaves it [1543](#cite:1543) [1545](#cite:1545).

name: DEPSCoR-eligible state or territory
what: An [institution of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) may apply to DEPSCoR only if it is in a state or territory on the list in the year's notice [1565](#cite:1565). The DEPSCoR list has 36 entries [1565](#cite:1565); the [NSF](#term:nsf) [EPSCoR](#term:epscor) list has 28 [1517](#cite:1517).
who_qualifies: For the FY26 notices posted August 10, 2026: Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, District of Columbia, Guam, Hawaii, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Oregon, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, U.S. Virgin Islands, Vermont, West Virginia, Wisconsin and Wyoming [1565](#cite:1565) [1566](#cite:1566).
how_decided: The list is published in each year's notice; the listings fetched do not state the rule that produces it [1565](#cite:1565).

name: DOE EPSCoR jurisdiction
what: DOE [EPSCoR](#term:epscor) takes applications only from applicants in designated states and territories, and it currently follows the [NSF](#term:nsf) EPSCoR eligibility criteria [1567](#cite:1567).
who_qualifies: Twenty-five states, Puerto Rico, Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands: Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Delaware, Guam, Hawaii, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Vermont, Virgin Islands, West Virginia and Wyoming [1567](#cite:1567). The same 28 are listed in the FY 2026 notice issued February 18, 2026 [1568](#cite:1568).
how_decided: By reference to the NSF EPSCoR eligibility criteria [1567](#cite:1567).

name: NASA EPSCoR jurisdiction
what: NASA [EPSCoR](#term:epscor) is open to institutions in jurisdictions that have not taken part equably in competitive aerospace research; twenty-five states, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands and Guam take part [1570](#cite:1570).
who_qualifies: As listed in the FY 2025 notices (posted October and November 2024): Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Delaware, Guam, Hawaii, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, U.S. Virgin Islands, Vermont, West Virginia and Wyoming [1573](#cite:1573) [1574](#cite:1574).
how_decided: Jurisdiction eligibility is determined by [NSF](#term:nsf); the FY 2025 notice used the 2023 NSF eligibility table [1574](#cite:1574).

name: USDA EPSCoR state (AFRI FASE)
what: State Agricultural Experiment Stations and degree-granting institutions in a USDA [EPSCoR](#term:epscor) state are eligible for [AFRI](#term:nifa) Strengthening [Grants](#term:grant) [1576](#cite:1576). The list is labelled by fiscal year and is not the [NSF](#term:nsf) list [1576](#cite:1576) [1517](#cite:1517).
who_qualifies: For FY 2026, 19 states: Alaska, Connecticut, Delaware, Hawaii, Idaho, Kentucky, Maine, Montana, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, North Dakota, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Utah, Vermont, West Virginia and Wyoming; also the District of Columbia, American Samoa, Guam, Micronesia, Northern Marianas, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands (page last updated March 13, 2026) [1576](#cite:1576).
how_decided: A state qualifies when its funding is no higher than the 38th [percentile](#term:percentile) of all states on a three-year rolling average of AFRI funding levels [1576](#cite:1576).

name: NIH SuRE-eligible institution
what: The class of higher education institution that may apply for SuRE and SuRE-First (R16) awards, defined by a ceiling on [NIH](#term:nih) research project [grant](#term:grant) funding and a floor on the share of students with Pell grants [1555](#cite:1555).
who_qualifies: A higher education institution that awards undergraduate (B.S. or B.A.) or graduate degrees in biomedical sciences, received no more than $6 million per year (total costs) from NIH Research Project Grants in each of the preceding two fiscal years, and enrols at least 25% of undergraduate students supported by Pell grants, on the most recent two years [1555](#cite:1555) [1556](#cite:1556).
how_decided: By the conditions in the notice; the fetch did not return how the institution documents them [1555](#cite:1555).

pending_changes.text: The FY 2026 notice is titled for programmes under section 312 only, where the FY 2025 notice was titled for Parts A and F of [Title III](#term:title-iii-v-eligibility) and Title V [1596](#cite:1596) [1597](#cite:1597).

name: Eligible institution under section 312 of the Higher Education Act (Title III and Title V eligibility designation)
what: An "eligible institution" is a college that enrols a high share of needy students and has low core expenses per student compared with institutions of its type [1596](#cite:1596). The Department of Education makes the designation each year; a designated institution may apply for the [grant](#term:grant) programmes that require it and may receive a one-year waiver of certain non-Federal [cost-sharing](#term:cost-sharing) requirements [1595](#cite:1595).
who_qualifies: At least 50 percent of degree-seeking students received Pell, FSEOG or Federal Work-Study aid, or the institution's Pell percentage exceeds the median for comparable institutions; and Core Expenses per FTE are below the average for the institution type [1596](#cite:1596). For FY 2026 (base year 2023-2024) the thresholds are: 2-year public 44% and $19,004; 2-year non-profit private 48% and $17,453; 4-year public 37% and $39,350; 4-year non-profit private 36% and $50,027 [1596](#cite:1596).
how_decided: The Department pre-determines eligibility from IPEDS data in the Eligibility Matrix; an institution checks its status in the Grant Eligibility Application system at HEPIS.ed.gov and, if not shown as eligible, applies for reconsideration or a waiver within the yearly window [1596](#cite:1596). The FY 2026 window ran from March 24 to April 23, 2026 [1596](#cite:1596). The FY 2025 Eligibility Matrix, with programme lists for the minority-serving classes, [HBCUs](#term:hbcu) and TCCUs, is published as an Excel file on the Department's eligibility page [1595](#cite:1595).

pending_changes.text: [Executive Order](#term:executive-order) 14283 set up a White House Initiative on [HBCUs](#term:hbcu) and directs agencies to file annual plans; it revoked Executive Order 14041 [1618](#cite:1618).

name: Historically Black college or university (Part B institution)
what: A historically Black college or university is an institution established before 1964 whose principal mission was the education of Black Americans, authorised by its state and accredited or preaccredited [1602](#cite:1602). The class is closed: it is fixed by statute and by a list in regulation, not by current enrolment [1649](#cite:1649).
who_qualifies: Institutions that satisfy section 322(2) of the Higher Education Act; 34 [CFR](#term:cfr) 608.2 lists them by state (the fetch counted 105) [1649](#cite:1649).
how_decided: Set by statute and listed in the Department of Education's regulation at 34 CFR 608.2 [1602](#cite:1602) [1649](#cite:1649). Executive Order 14283 defines the term by reference to that list, and the Defense and [NIH](#term:nih) notices read in this sweep use the same statutory definition [1618](#cite:1618) [1627](#cite:1627) [1656](#cite:1656). The Department's FY 2025 Eligibility Matrix also carries an HBCU list [1595](#cite:1595).

name: Historically Black Graduate Institution (section 326)
what: The 24 institutions and schools named in section 326 of the Higher Education Act, such as Morehouse School of Medicine and Meharry Medical College [1603](#cite:1603).
who_qualifies: Only the institutions named in the statute; the Department's page lists all 24 [1603](#cite:1603).
how_decided: Set by statute, 20 U.S.C. 1063b [1603](#cite:1603).

pending_changes.text: The Justice Department told Congress it would not defend 20 U.S.C. 1101(c) and the 25 percent definition in 20 U.S.C. 1101a(5)(B) in State of Tennessee v. U.S. Department of Education [1606](#cite:1606).
The Office of Legal Counsel concluded that the Department of Education's three [HSI](#term:hispanic-serving-institution) programmes are unconstitutional and inseverable [1592](#cite:1592).
A law firm summary of September 30, 2026 reports that the court had not ruled on the intervenor's motions and that plaintiffs moved for summary judgment on August 31, 2026 [1650](#cite:1650).

The FY 2026 eligibility designation notice covers programmes under section 312 only, and no FY 2026 eligibility process for [Title V](#term:title-iii-v-eligibility) was found [1596](#cite:1596) [1597](#cite:1597).

name: Hispanic-serving institution (HSI)
what: A Hispanic-serving institution is an eligible institution under Title V whose undergraduate full-time-equivalent enrolment is at least 25 percent Hispanic at the end of the award year before it applies [1647](#cite:1647). The status follows enrolment and is shown when an institution applies; it is not a permanent list [1642](#cite:1642).
who_qualifies: An institution that meets the eligible-institution tests (needy students, low educational and general expenditures, accreditation) and the 25 percent enrolment test [1647](#cite:1647).
how_decided: In the Department of Education's last competition the applicant documented the 25 percent at application and the Department checked it against IPEDS and other data, with the burden on the institution to show IPEDS data are inaccurate [1642](#cite:1642). The FY 2025 Eligibility Matrix includes a list of institutions meeting the HSI definition [1595](#cite:1595). [NSF](#term:nsf)'s archived [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) required an eligibility letter from the Department of Education, and the agricultural research statute adopts the same definition [1609](#cite:1609) [1640](#cite:1640).

pending_changes.text: [Executive Order](#term:executive-order) 14148 revoked Executive Order 14049 of October 11, 2021, which had set up a White House initiative that included strengthening [tribal colleges](#term:tribal-college) and universities [1619](#cite:1619).
The Office of Legal Counsel concluded that [NSF](#term:nsf) awards to tribal colleges fall within the Morton v. Mancari exception and are constitutional [876](#cite:876).

name: Tribal college or university (TCU / TCCU)
what: A tribal college or university is an institution that qualifies under the Tribally Controlled College or University Assistance Act of 1978 or the Navajo Community College Assistance Act of 1978, or is named in section 532 of the Equity in Educational [Land-Grant](#term:land-grant-institution) Status Act of 1994 [1617](#cite:1617).
who_qualifies: Institutions meeting one of those statutory tests; section 532 names 36 colleges in the 2023 edition of the United States Code [1617](#cite:1617) [1641](#cite:1641).
how_decided: Set by statute; for the Department of Education programme a new applicant needs an eligibility determination from the Bureau of Indian Education, and existing grantees no longer apply for eligibility [1617](#cite:1617). NSF uses the section 532 list and the 1978 Act for its Tribal Colleges and Universities Program [1613](#cite:1613).

pending_changes.text: The Office of Legal Counsel concluded that the Department of Education programme for this class is unconstitutional and inseverable [1592](#cite:1592).

name: Alaska Native-serving or Native Hawaiian-serving institution (ANNH)
what: An Alaska Native-serving institution is an eligible institution whose undergraduate enrolment is at least 20 percent Alaska Native at the time of application; a Native Hawaiian-serving institution is one with at least 10 percent Native Hawaiian undergraduates [1646](#cite:1646).
who_qualifies: Eligible institutions under 20 U.S.C. 1058(b) that meet the enrolment share [1646](#cite:1646).
how_decided: By enrolment at the time of application, documented in the Department of Education's last notice by an assurance form signed by an official of the applicant [1646](#cite:1646). [NSF](#term:nsf) applies the same percentages for its [Tribal Colleges](#term:tribal-college) and Universities Program [1613](#cite:1613).

pending_changes.text: The Office of Legal Counsel concluded that the Department of Education programme for this class is unconstitutional and inseverable [1592](#cite:1592).

name: Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-serving institution (AANAPISI)
what: An AANAPISI is an eligible institution whose enrolment is at least 10 percent Asian American or Native American Pacific Islander [1644](#cite:1644).
who_qualifies: Eligible institutions that meet the 10 percent enrolment share [1644](#cite:1644).
how_decided: By enrolment, certified by the applicant at application in the Department of Education's last notice [1644](#cite:1644).

pending_changes.text: The Office of Legal Counsel concluded that the Department of Education programme for this class is unconstitutional and inseverable [1592](#cite:1592).

name: Native American-serving nontribal institution (NASNTI)
what: A Native American-serving nontribal institution is an eligible institution, not a [tribal college](#term:tribal-college), whose enrolment is not less than 10 percent Native American [1645](#cite:1645).
who_qualifies: Eligible institutions that meet the 10 percent share and are not tribal colleges [1645](#cite:1645).
how_decided: By enrolment, certified by the applicant at application in the Department of Education's last notice [1645](#cite:1645).

pending_changes.text: The Office of Legal Counsel concluded that the PBI formula programme is unconstitutional and inseverable [1592](#cite:1592).

name: Predominantly Black Institution (PBI)
what: A Predominantly Black Institution is an eligible institution with at least 1,000 undergraduates, at least 40 percent Black American students, and at least half of its undergraduates low-income or first-generation and enrolled in bachelor's or associate's degree programmes [1648](#cite:1648).
who_qualifies: Institutions meeting the tests in 20 U.S.C. 1059e [1648](#cite:1648).
how_decided: By the statutory tests, on application to the Secretary of Education [1648](#cite:1648). The FY 2025 Eligibility Matrix includes a PBI list [1595](#cite:1595).

name: 1862 land-grant institution
what: The 1862 [land-grant institutions](#term:land-grant-institution) are the public universities eligible for funds under the Act of July 2, 1862 (the First Morrill Act) [1640](#cite:1640) [1636](#cite:1636).
who_qualifies: Institutions eligible to receive funds under the 1862 Act [1640](#cite:1640).
how_decided: Set by statute; [NIFA](#term:nifa) publishes a directory of land-grant colleges and universities [1640](#cite:1640) [1636](#cite:1636).

name: 1890 land-grant institution
what: The 1890 [land-grant institutions](#term:land-grant-institution) are historically Black universities established under the Second Morrill Act of 1890, together with Tuskegee University [1637](#cite:1637) [1640](#cite:1640).
who_qualifies: [NIFA](#term:nifa) lists 19 universities, including Central State University and West Virginia State University [1637](#cite:1637).
how_decided: Set by statute; NIFA publishes the list [1640](#cite:1640) [1637](#cite:1637).

name: 1994 land-grant institution (tribal college)
what: The 1994 Institutions are the [tribal colleges](#term:tribal-college) named in section 532 of the Equity in Educational [Land-Grant](#term:land-grant-institution) Status Act of 1994, which the Act treats as land-grant colleges [1641](#cite:1641).
who_qualifies: The colleges named in section 532; the 2023 edition of the Code lists 36 [1641](#cite:1641).
how_decided: Set by statute; a college is added by amendment of section 532 [1641](#cite:1641).

name: Non-land-grant college of agriculture (NLGCA), certified by NIFA
what: A non-land-grant college of agriculture is a public institution, outside the [land-grant](#term:land-grant-institution) system, that offers a bachelor's or higher degree in agriculture, forestry or a related field [1640](#cite:1640).
who_qualifies: Institutions certified as NLGCAs by [NIFA](#term:nifa) [1659](#cite:1659).
how_decided: NIFA certifies institutions and posts the certified list on its site [1659](#cite:1659).

name: Community college or two-year institution, as programmes define it
what: There is no single federal designation of a community college; each programme states its own test [1621](#cite:1621) [1615](#cite:1615).
who_qualifies: The Labor Department's Strengthening Community Colleges [grants](#term:grant) require a lead applicant that is an institution under section 101(a) of the Higher Education Act at which the associate degree is primarily the highest degree awarded [1621](#cite:1621). [NSF](#term:nsf)'s Advanced Technological Education programme names accredited two- and four-year institutions, including community colleges, and centres on two-year institutions [1615](#cite:1615) [1614](#cite:1614). The Department of Education's eligibility thresholds are set separately for two-year public and two-year non-profit private institutions [1596](#cite:1596).
how_decided: By each notice's own definition; no list is published [1621](#cite:1621) [1615](#cite:1615).

name: Covered educational institution (Department of Defense HBCU/MI programme)
what: The Defense programme for historically Black colleges and universities and [minority-serving institutions](#term:minority-serving-institution) supports "covered educational institutions" under 10 U.S.C. 4144 [1625](#cite:1625).
who_qualifies: The Navy's FY 2027 notice defines them as institutions eligible under [Title III](#term:title-iii-v-eligibility) or V of the Higher Education Act, or accredited postsecondary minority institutions [1628](#cite:1628). The 2026 equipment notice is narrower: Part B institutions and [tribal colleges](#term:tribal-college) only [1627](#cite:1627).
how_decided: By statute and by each notice [1625](#cite:1625) [1628](#cite:1628).

name: RCMI-eligible institution
what: For Research Centers in Minority Institutions, [NIH](#term:nih) set an institutional test that combines degrees awarded, mission and a ceiling on NIH funding [1622](#cite:1622).
who_qualifies: Under RFA-MD-24-012: a domestic higher education institution that awards doctorates in the health professions or health-related sciences, has a documented historical mission or commitment to educating underrepresented students, and received less than $50 million a year of NIH support, or less than $25 million a year of [R01](#term:r01) total costs, over the past three fiscal years [1622](#cite:1622).
how_decided: Stated in the notice and documented by the applicant; the notice has expired [1622](#cite:1622).

name: NASA MSI List
what: NASA checks eligibility for its Minority University Research and Education Project against the NASA [MSI](#term:minority-serving-institution) List on the MSI Exchange site [1629](#cite:1629).
who_qualifies: Institutions on the list [1629](#cite:1629).
how_decided: The list is drawn from Department of Education Office of Postsecondary Education data, updated yearly with data from two years before [1629](#cite:1629).

name: Recipient named by Congress for a Community Project Funding or Congressionally Directed Spending project
what: An organisation has this standing when an enacted [appropriations act](#term:appropriations-act)'s joint explanatory statement names it as the recipient of a specific project and amount [1686](#cite:1686). The agency then funds only the named entity, for the named purpose [1687](#cite:1687) [1690](#cite:1690).
who_qualifies: State, local and tribal governments and certain eligible non-profits may be named; for-profit entities may not [1667](#cite:1667) [1675](#cite:1675). Which non-profits may be named differs by account and by chamber: in FY27 the House names only colleges among non-profits in its science accounts, only certain rural and safety-net health providers at [HRSA](#term:hrsa), and no non-profits other than fire stations in Community Facilities [1671](#cite:1671) [1670](#cite:1670) [1672](#cite:1672).
how_decided: By Congress, on a request from a Member or Senator who certifies no financial interest and posts the request online; the standing lasts for that act's project only [1667](#cite:1667) [1675](#cite:1675).

name: Organisation named in Section 4 of the HUD Demonstration Act of 1993
what: Section 4 capacity-building money may go only to the non-profits identified in Section 4 of the HUD Demonstration Act of 1993 [1712](#cite:1712).
who_qualifies: Enterprise Community Partners, Inc., Local Initiatives Support Corporation and Habitat for Humanity International; their affiliates, local offices and community partners do not qualify [1712](#cite:1712) [1713](#cite:1713).
how_decided: Set by statute [1712](#cite:1712).

name: Emerging CDFI (and NACA Sponsoring Entity)
what: An Emerging [CDFI](#term:cdfi) is an organisation not yet certified that shows the CDFI Fund, in its application, an acceptable plan to meet the certification requirements by the end of its [period of performance](#term:budget-period) [1434](#cite:1434). In the NACA Program a Sponsoring Entity is an organisation primarily serving Native communities that proposes to create a separate Certified CDFI [1717](#cite:1717).
who_qualifies: A non-certified entity with such a plan; under the FY 2025 notice an Emerging CDFI that wins a Technical Assistance award must be certified by the date in its Assistance Agreement [1434](#cite:1434). A Sponsoring Entity proposes to create the CDFI within four years [1717](#cite:1717).
how_decided: By the CDFI Fund, from the application [1434](#cite:1434).

name: Nationally significant property or collection (Save America's Treasures)
what: Save America's Treasures preservation [grants](#term:grant) are for properties listed in the National Register of Historic Places for national significance or designated a National Historic Landmark; collections grants are for nationally significant collections [1695](#cite:1695) [1696](#cite:1696).
who_qualifies: The owner or steward of such a property or collection that has not had a Save America's Treasures grant before [1695](#cite:1695).
how_decided: By the property's National Register listing or National Historic Landmark designation, and for a collection by the reviewers' score on the national significance criterion, worth 25 of 100 points [1695](#cite:1695) [1705](#cite:1705).

name: Accredited HBCU with a National Register-eligible building
what: Only accredited Historically Black Colleges and Universities may apply for the National Park Service's [HBCU](#term:hbcu) preservation [grants](#term:grant) [1699](#cite:1699).
who_qualifies: An accredited HBCU whose building is listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places, individually or as contributing to a historic district, or is a National Historic Landmark [1699](#cite:1699) [1698](#cite:1698).
how_decided: By the institution's accreditation and the property's National Register status, as the notice states [1699](#cite:1699).

name: State Historical Records Advisory Board (SHRAB)
what: A State Historical Records Advisory Board is the body, authorised by a state, a territory or the District of Columbia, that may apply for the Commission's State Board Programming [Grants](#term:grant) [700](#cite:700).
who_qualifies: Boards authorised by any of the U.S. states or territories and the District of Columbia [700](#cite:700).
how_decided: By the state's or territory's authorisation of the board [700](#cite:700).

name: Existing Health Center Program awardee (for capital funding)
what: [HRSA](#term:hrsa)'s 2021 capital notice was open only to existing health centres receiving Health Center Program operational support under sections 330(e), (g), (h) or (i) at the time of application and award [1738](#cite:1738).
who_qualifies: A health centre already funded under those sections; the pack's records `hrsa-health-center-service-area-competition` and `hrsa-health-center-new-access-points` are the routes to that funding [1738](#cite:1738).
how_decided: By holding a Health Center Program award [1738](#cite:1738).

name: Low-risk auditee
what: A low-risk auditee is an organisation whose last two [single audits](#term:single-audit) were clean enough to earn reduced audit coverage [1847](#cite:1847). The status also lets a recipient self-certify a higher micro-purchase threshold for its own purchasing [1819](#cite:1819).
who_qualifies: An auditee that, for each of the two preceding audit periods, had annual single audits filed with the [Federal Audit Clearinghouse](#term:federal-audit-clearinghouse) on time; unmodified auditor's opinions on the financial statements and on the schedule of expenditures of federal awards; no material weaknesses in internal control; no going-concern doubt; and none of the listed findings in its Type A programmes [1847](#cite:1847). An entity audited every two years does not qualify [1847](#cite:1847).
how_decided: Determined by the auditor against the conditions in [2 CFR 200](#term:uniform-guidance).520 during each single audit [1847](#cite:1847).

name: Organisation without a current federally negotiated indirect cost rate
what: An organisation in this position may charge [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) at the [de minimis rate](#term:de-minimis-rate) without negotiating, or may submit a proposal to its [cognizant agency](#term:cognizant-agency) [1802](#cite:1802) [163](#cite:163). Many small non-profits and first-time recipients are in it [1802](#cite:1802).
who_qualifies: Any recipient or [subrecipient](#term:subrecipient) that does not have a current federal [negotiated indirect cost rate](#term:nicra) [1802](#cite:1802). The rate is up to 15 percent of [modified total direct costs](#term:mtdc) and may be used indefinitely [1802](#cite:1802).
how_decided: By the organisation's own election under [2 CFR 200](#term:uniform-guidance).414(f); no documentation is required to justify the rate [1802](#cite:1802). The award document records that the de minimis rate is charged [1810](#cite:1810).

name: Cognizant agency for indirect costs
what: Each organisation that negotiates an [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) rate has one federal agency that reviews, negotiates and approves its proposal on behalf of all federal agencies [1799](#cite:1799). Which agency it is follows from the kind of organisation and where its federal money comes from [1849](#cite:1849) [1850](#cite:1850).
who_qualifies: For an [institution of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education): [HHS](#term:hhs) or the Department of Defense's Office of Naval Research, normally whichever provided more funds directly to the institution for the most recent three years; the assignment continues for five years [1849](#cite:1849). For a non-profit organisation: the federal agency with the largest dollar value of awards directly funded to the organisation [1850](#cite:1850).
how_decided: Set by Appendix III and Appendix IV to [2 CFR part 200](#term:uniform-guidance) [1849](#cite:1849) [1850](#cite:1850). The same agency approves a micro-purchase threshold above $50,000 [1819](#cite:1819).

name: Non-profit receiving more than $10 million in direct federal funding in a fiscal year
what: A non-profit above this level must state its [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) rate in two parts, Facilities and Administration, as universities do [1850](#cite:1850) [1802](#cite:1802).
who_qualifies: An organisation that receives more than $10 million in direct federal funding in a fiscal year [1850]. ONR publishes separate guidance for non-profits with less than $10M annual direct federal funding [1861](#cite:1861).
how_decided: By the amount of direct federal funding in the fiscal year, under Appendix IV to [2 CFR part 200](#term:uniform-guidance) [1850](#cite:1850).

pending_changes.text: [OMB](#term:omb)'s [proposed rule](#term:proposed-rule) lists a revision to 200.331 [1458](#cite:1458).

name: Subrecipient (as against contractor)
what: A [subrecipient](#term:subrecipient) receives a [subaward](#term:subaward) from a [pass-through entity](#term:pass-through-entity) to carry out part of a federal award, and the federal terms flow down to it [1799](#cite:1799) [1805](#cite:1805). A contractor sells goods or services to the recipient and is not subject to the programme's compliance requirements [1822](#cite:1822). The classification decides whether the money counts toward the [single audit](#term:single-audit) threshold [1845](#cite:1845).
who_qualifies: An entity that determines who is eligible for assistance, has its performance measured against programme objectives, makes programmatic decisions, is responsible for programme requirements, and implements a programme for a public purpose [1822](#cite:1822).
how_decided: Case by case by the pass-through entity under [2 CFR 200](#term:uniform-guidance).331, on the substance of the relationship [1822](#cite:1822).

name: Organisation recognised as tax-exempt under section 501(c)(3)
what: The standing that federal notices describe as "nonprofits having a [501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) status with the IRS" [2064](#cite:2064). It is held by an organisation that the IRS has recognised as exempt, normally on an application on [Form 1023](#term:form-1023) or Form 1023-EZ [2046](#cite:2046).
who_qualifies: An organisation formed under state law as a trust, corporation or association that has applied and been recognised [2047](#cite:2047) [2046](#cite:2046). A subordinate covered by a central organisation's [group exemption letter](#term:group-exemption) holds the status without its own application [2060](#cite:2060). Some agencies ask for this status by name: the Arts Endowment requires a non-profit applicant to be a tax-exempt 501(c)(3) entity, and a 2026 [NEH](#term:neh) notice requires recognition under section 501(c)(3) [2065](#cite:2065) [648](#cite:648).
how_decided: By IRS [determination letter](#term:determination-letter) [2059](#cite:2059). A funder checks the [Tax Exempt Organization Search](#term:tax-exempt-organization-search), which holds the list of organisations eligible for deductible contributions, determination letters, filed returns and the [Automatic Revocation List](#term:automatic-revocation) [2059](#cite:2059). An organisation can ask the IRS for an affirmation letter confirming its status [2066](#cite:2066). The status is lost automatically after three consecutive years without an annual return or notice [2057](#cite:2057).

name: Non-profit without 501(c)(3) status (Grants.gov applicant category)
what: [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) lists two non-profit applicant categories: those having [501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) status with the IRS and those that do not, each other than [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) [2064](#cite:2064). The Grants.gov page gives the second category's wording and no further definition [2064](#cite:2064).
who_qualifies: The IRS states that state law governs non-profit status and federal law governs tax-exempt status, so an organisation can be a non-profit under state law without IRS recognition under section 501(c)(3) [2047](#cite:2047). Organisations exempt under other paragraphs of section 501(c) apply on Form 1024 or Form 1024-A [2046](#cite:2046). Whether a given notice admits the category is stated in that notice's eligibility section [2064](#cite:2064).
how_decided: By the eligibility list of each notice [2064](#cite:2064). The pack's record nih-nonprofit-other-than-higher-education holds [NIH](#term:nih)'s use of the two categories [2064](#cite:2064).

name: Public charity (as against private foundation)
what: Every [section 501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) organisation is classified as either a [private foundation](#term:private-foundation) or a [public charity](#term:public-charity) [2054](#cite:2054). The classification decides which annual return the organisation files and which restrictions apply to it [2054](#cite:2054) [2055](#cite:2055).
who_qualifies: An organisation is presumed to be a private foundation unless it requests and qualifies for a determination as a public charity [2054](#cite:2054). Public charities include churches, schools, hospitals, [medical research organisations](#term:medical-research-organization), publicly supported organisations that receive a specified portion of their support from public sources, and certain [supporting organisations](#term:supporting-organization) [2054](#cite:2054).
how_decided: By the IRS, on the organisation's application [2054](#cite:2054). For a [grant](#term:grant) seeker the difference shows in three places the IRS pages state: a private foundation files [Form 990-PF](#term:form-990-pf) whatever its size, it is subject to operating restrictions and excise taxes, and the short [Form 1023-EZ](#term:form-1023) is closed to private [operating foundations](#term:operating-foundation) and supporting organisations [2055](#cite:2055) [2054](#cite:2054) [2050](#cite:2050). Under the 2026 [group exemption](#term:group-exemption) procedure, section 501(c)(3) subordinates must be public charities [2061](#cite:2061).

pending_changes.text: Revenue Procedure 2026-8 superseded Revenue Procedure 80-27, and the IRS resumed accepting [group exemption](#term:group-exemption) applications after January 20, 2026; existing holders have transition periods whose dates were not returned by the fetch [2061](#cite:2061).

name: Subordinate organisation under a group exemption letter
what: A group exemption letter lets a central organisation obtain recognition of exemption for the subordinate organisations under its general supervision or control; a subordinate included in the letter does not file its own application [2060](#cite:2060).
who_qualifies: Subordinates must all be described in the same paragraph of section 501(c) [2060](#cite:2060). A central organisation needs at least five subordinates to obtain a letter and at least one to keep it [2060](#cite:2060). Under Revenue Procedure 2026-8, as returned by the fetch, [section 501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) subordinates must be [public charities](#term:public-charity) with the same foundation classification and foreign subordinates are not permitted [2061](#cite:2061).
how_decided: By the IRS's group exemption letter to the central organisation, under Revenue Procedure 2026-8, published in Internal Revenue Bulletin 2026-04 on January 20, 2026 [2060](#cite:2060) [2061](#cite:2061).
