The IRS pages read do not say how a funder verifies that a particular subordinate is covered [2060](#cite:2060).

name: Project under a fiscal sponsor
what: A [fiscal sponsor](#term:fiscal-sponsorship), in the Arts Endowment's words, is an entity that oversees the fiscal activities of another organisation, company, or group of independent artists or projects [2065](#cite:2065). The two federal pages read in this sweep do not accept an application made that way [2065](#cite:2065) [648](#cite:648).
who_qualifies: Arts Endowment: an organisation without its own non-profit status may not use a fiscal sponsor or agent to submit an application; it may take part in a project submitted by an eligible organisation, and a fiscal sponsor may apply for its own programme activities [2065](#cite:2065). [NEH](#term:neh), in a notice of March 12, 2026: a recipient may not function solely as a fiscal agent, fiscal sponsors applying on behalf of an ineligible organisation are not eligible, and fiscal agent fees are [unallowable](#term:allowable-cost) [648](#cite:648).
how_decided: By each agency's eligibility rules [2065](#cite:2065) [648](#cite:648). No IRS page read in this sweep describes fiscal sponsorship, and no page was found in which a federal agency accepts a fiscally sponsored applicant; other agencies' rules were not checked [2047](#cite:2047).

name: Covered institution (research security programme)
what: The class of institution that must certify a [research security programme](#term:research-security): an [institution of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education), a federally funded research and development centre or a non-profit research institution receiving in excess of $50 million per year in federal research and development funding [2017](#cite:2017).
who_qualifies: The amount is a three-year average of federal research and development obligations in fiscal year 2022 constant dollars [2017](#cite:2017). NSPM-33 states the threshold as Federal science and engineering support in excess of 50 million dollars per year [247](#cite:247).
how_decided: By the threshold in the OSTP memorandum of July 9, 2024 [2017](#cite:2017). No published list of covered institutions was found in this sweep [2018](#cite:2018).

name: Small institution (research misconduct assurance)
what: An institution too small to run a research misconduct inquiry or investigation without a conflict of interest may, with ORI's approval, file a Small Institution Statement in place of its own policies and procedures (42 [CFR](#term:cfr) 93.303) [2007](#cite:2007) [2010](#cite:2010).
who_qualifies: ORI describes small institutions as typically 1 to 50 institutional members [2010](#cite:2010).
how_decided: By ORI, on the institution's statement, filed as a fillable PDF in the 2026.03 version [2010](#cite:2010). The institution still reports all allegations to ORI and files the annual report [2010](#cite:2010) [2007](#cite:2007).

name: Institution invited to nominate for a foundation fellowship
what: Some foundation fellowships are closed to all but a list of institutions the funder has chosen. A researcher elsewhere cannot enter, whatever the merit of the work [2149](#cite:2149) [2174](#cite:2174).
who_qualifies: Packard Fellowships: 50 invited institutions in 2026 [2149](#cite:2149). Pew Scholars: 212 participating institutions were listed for the 2027 award [2174](#cite:2174). Mellon New Directions Fellowships: invited institutions, with no guarantee of a further invitation [2212](#cite:2212). Schmidt Science Polymaths: a select group of nominating institutions [2153](#cite:2153).
how_decided: By the funder; none of the pages read gives a way for an institution to ask to be added [2149](#cite:2149) [2174](#cite:2174) [2212](#cite:2212).

name: HHMI-eligible institution
what: HHMI appoints scientists only at institutions on its own list of eligible institutions [2161](#cite:2161) [2162](#cite:2162).
who_qualifies: The list was not read in this sweep; the programme pages require that a candidate hold, or be about to start, a position at an HHMI-eligible institution [2162](#cite:2162) [2163](#cite:2163).
how_decided: By HHMI [2161](#cite:2161).

name: Knight community
what: One of the 26 communities 'where John S. and James L. Knight once owned and operated newspapers'; the Knight Foundation's community funding and its Knight Cities Challenge are limited to them [2296](#cite:2296) [2355](#cite:2355).
who_qualifies: Aberdeen SD, Akron OH, Biloxi MS, Boulder CO, Bradenton FL, Charlotte NC, Columbia SC, Columbus GA, Detroit MI, Duluth MN, Fort Wayne IN, Gary IN, Grand Forks ND, Lexington KY, Long Beach CA, Macon GA, Miami FL, Milledgeville GA, Myrtle Beach SC, Palm Beach County FL, Philadelphia PA, San Jose CA, St. Paul MN, State College PA, Tallahassee FL and Wichita KS [2355](#cite:2355).
how_decided: Fixed by the foundation's history; the list is the foundation's own [2296](#cite:2296).

name: Organisation eligible for The Duke Endowment
what: The Duke Endowment funds only certain kinds of organisation in North Carolina and South Carolina, set by programme area under its founding trust document [2309](#cite:2309) [2310](#cite:2310).
who_qualifies: Health care: not-for-profit hospitals, academic health centres, area health education centres and select organisations in underserved counties of the two states [2363](#cite:2363). Child and family: accredited organisations and other non-profit groups in the two states serving children and families who have experienced or are at risk of child maltreatment [2310](#cite:2310). Higher education: Davidson College, Duke University, Furman University and Johnson C. Smith University [2362](#cite:2362). The rule for the Rural Church area was not read [2309](#cite:2309).
how_decided: By the Endowment, under the trust document of James B. Duke [2310](#cite:2310).

name: W. K. Kellogg Foundation priority place
what: The Kellogg Foundation names places where it concentrates its grantmaking; 58 percent of its new commitments in the fiscal year ending August 31, 2024 benefited them [2269](#cite:2269) [2345](#cite:2345).
who_qualifies: Michigan, Mississippi, New Mexico and New Orleans in the United States; Chiapas and the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico; central and southwest Haiti [2269](#cite:2269).
how_decided: Set by the foundation; work outside the priority places is not excluded [2345](#cite:2345).

name: Private foundation (as against a public charity)
what: Under the tax code every [section 501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) organisation is a [private foundation](#term:private-foundation) unless it falls into a category the law excludes [2237](#cite:2237). The excluded organisations are the [public charities](#term:public-charity): churches, hospitals, schools, colleges and universities, organisations with many sources of support, and organisations that support them [2238](#cite:2238). A private foundation files [Form 990-PF](#term:form-990-pf) each year and is subject to a set of excise taxes that a public charity is not [2237](#cite:2237) [2387](#cite:2387).
who_qualifies: Any section 501(c)(3) organisation that does not fall into one of the excluded categories; the IRS names hospitals, universities and organisations with broad public support or in a supporting relationship as excluded [2237](#cite:2237).
how_decided: Set by statute as the default class, and recorded by the IRS when it recognises the exemption; a private foundation states its type in item H on page 1 of Form 990-PF [2237](#cite:2237) [2387](#cite:2387).
for_grant_seekers: A private foundation's [grant](#term:grant) to a public charity is not a taxable expenditure, while its grant to any other organisation is one unless the foundation exercises [expenditure responsibility](#term:expenditure-responsibility) [2380](#cite:2380). Its return is public and lists every grant paid, so a reader can see what it has funded [2387](#cite:2387) [2461](#cite:2461).

name: Private non-operating foundation (the grantmaking kind)
what: A [private foundation](#term:private-foundation) that is not an [operating foundation](#term:operating-foundation) is a nonoperating foundation in IRS statistics, which report that nonoperating foundations filed 91.2% of private foundation returns for tax year 2022 [2410](#cite:2410). This kind must meet the annual [minimum distribution](#term:minimum-distribution), computed from 5 percent of its investment assets [2377](#cite:2377) [2375](#cite:2375).
who_qualifies: A private foundation that does not meet the definition of a private operating foundation [2371](#cite:2371).
how_decided: By the tax code; the foundation computes its distributable amount in Parts IX to XII of [Form 990-PF](#term:form-990-pf) [2388](#cite:2388) [2387](#cite:2387).
for_grant_seekers: This kind must pay out a minimum amount each year [2375](#cite:2375). Whether it takes requests is a separate matter, shown on Part XIV, line 2 of its Form 990-PF [2387](#cite:2387).

name: Private operating foundation
what: A [private operating foundation](#term:operating-foundation) is a [private foundation](#term:private-foundation) that devotes most of its resources to the active conduct of its own exempt activities [2371](#cite:2371). It is not subject to the excise tax on failure to distribute income, and it still pays the tax on net investment income and follows the other private foundation rules [2371](#cite:2371).
who_qualifies: A private foundation that devotes most of its resources to the active conduct of its exempt activities; the IRS sets out the tests on linked pages that this sweep did not read [2371](#cite:2371).
how_decided: By tests in the tax code; a foundation claiming the status completes Part XIII of [Form 990-PF](#term:form-990-pf), titled Private Operating Foundations [2388](#cite:2388).
for_grant_seekers: An operating foundation devotes most of its resources to its own activities [2371](#cite:2371). Any [grants](#term:grant) it paid still appear in Part XIV, line 3 of its Form 990-PF [2387](#cite:2387).

name: Community foundation (community trust)
what: The IRS's term is [community trust](#term:community-foundation): a charity that attracts large contributions for the benefit of a particular community or area [2374](#cite:2374). A community trust that meets a public support test is a [public charity](#term:public-charity), not a [private foundation](#term:private-foundation), and says so on Schedule A of [Form 990](#term:form-990) [2374](#cite:2374). The Council on Foundations describes community foundations as grantmaking public charities serving a defined local area and counts more than 900 of them [2405](#cite:2405).
who_qualifies: A community trust that meets a section 170(b)(1)(A)(vi) public support test checks line 8 in Part I of Schedule A and completes Part II [2374](#cite:2374). The Greater Kansas City Community Foundation's 2024 Form 990 checks that line [2432](#cite:2432).
how_decided: By the public support test in the tax code, reported each year on Schedule A of Form 990 [2374](#cite:2374).
for_grant_seekers: A community foundation files Form 990, not [Form 990-PF](#term:form-990-pf), so it has no Part XIV line on [unsolicited requests](#term:unsolicited-request); its own website is the place to learn how it takes applications [2374](#cite:2374) [2432](#cite:2432). Much of what a community foundation pays out can be advised by donors and not open to application: the Greater Kansas City Community Foundation says most of its donors hold [donor-advised funds](#term:donor-advised-fund) and make their own decisions [2428](#cite:2428).

name: Supporting organisation
what: A [supporting organisation](#term:supporting-organization) is a [public charity](#term:public-charity) because of its relationship to one or more other public charities that it supports [2238](#cite:2238). It must satisfy an organizational test, an operational test, a control test and a relationship test, and comes in three types [2372](#cite:2372).
who_qualifies: An organisation that meets the four tests; Type I is operated, supervised or controlled by its supported organisation, Type II is supervised or controlled in connection with it, and Type III is either functionally integrated or not [2372](#cite:2372).
how_decided: By the tests in the tax code, as the IRS sets them out [2372](#cite:2372).
for_grant_seekers: A supporting organisation functions in a supporting relationship to one or more existing public charities [2238](#cite:2238). A Type III organisation that is not functionally integrated has its own [payout](#term:minimum-distribution) rule: the greater of 85 percent of adjusted net income and 3.5 percent of the value of its non-exempt-use assets [2372](#cite:2372). Gifts to supporting organisations do not qualify for the new deduction for non-itemisers [2389](#cite:2389).

name: Donor-advised fund and its sponsoring organisation
what: A [donor-advised fund](#term:donor-advised-fund) is a separately identified fund or account that is maintained and operated by a [section 501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) organisation, called a sponsoring organisation [2373](#cite:2373). Once the donor gives, the sponsoring organisation has legal control of the money, and the donor or the donor's representative keeps advisory privileges over distributions and investments [2373](#cite:2373).
who_qualifies: The sponsoring organisation is a section 501(c)(3) organisation that maintains the funds; [community foundations](#term:community-foundation) are among them [2373](#cite:2373) [2428](#cite:2428).
how_decided: Defined in the tax code, as the IRS describes it [2373](#cite:2373).
for_grant_seekers: A [grant](#term:grant) from a donor-advised fund starts with the donor's advice, not with an application to the sponsor [2373](#cite:2373). The New York Community Trust tells applicants "We cannot refer you to donors" [2416](#cite:2416). The Greater Kansas City Community Foundation says its donors "make their own decisions regarding which nonprofits they support" and offers a non-profit a report of grants it has received from the foundation's funds since 1994 [2428](#cite:2428). Gifts to donor-advised funds do not qualify for the deduction for non-itemisers that begins with tax year 2026 [2389](#cite:2389).

name: Corporate foundation versus corporate giving programme
what: A company can give in two ways [2408](#cite:2408). A [company-sponsored foundation](#term:corporate-foundation) is a [private foundation](#term:private-foundation) whose assets come mainly from the contributions of a for-profit business, and a corporate giving programme is a grantmaking programme set up and run inside the company itself [2408](#cite:2408). Walmart shows both side by side: its local cash [grants](#term:grant) are awarded by Walmart U.S. stores, Sam's Clubs and Distribution Centers, while other giving is by Walmart and the Walmart Foundation by invitation [2435](#cite:2435) [2433](#cite:2433).
who_qualifies: The IRS pages read in this sweep do not define a corporate foundation as a class of its own; as a private foundation it falls under the general rule [2237](#cite:2237). The definitions here are Candid's [2408](#cite:2408).
how_decided: A corporate foundation is a separate legal body that files [Form 990-PF](#term:form-990-pf); a giving programme is part of the company and files no public return of its own [2408](#cite:2408) [2387](#cite:2387).
for_grant_seekers: The corporate funders read in this sweep show a pattern: an open route for small local grants or a fixed annual window, and national grants by invitation [2433](#cite:2433) [2441](#cite:2441) [2438](#cite:2438). Walmart states "[Unsolicited proposals](#term:unsolicited-request) will not be accepted, and invitations are not granted upon request" for everything but its local grants [2433](#cite:2433). Wells Fargo and the Wells Fargo Foundation "have implemented an invitation process" [2441](#cite:2441). Bank of America takes applications in two dated windows a year [2438](#cite:2438). From tax years beginning after December 31, 2025 a corporation may deduct charitable gifts only above 1 percent of taxable income [2392](#cite:2392) [2395](#cite:2395).

name: Medical research organisation
what: A [medical research organisation](#term:medical-research-organization) is a [public charity](#term:public-charity) whose principal purpose or function is to engage in medical research and that is directly engaged in the continuous active conduct of medical research in conjunction with a hospital [2374](#cite:2374). The IRS lists qualified medical research organisations affiliated with hospitals among the public charities [2238](#cite:2238).
who_qualifies: An organisation that meets the definition checks line 4 in Part I of Schedule A ([Form 990](#term:form-990)) [2374](#cite:2374).
how_decided: By the definition in the tax code, reported on Schedule A of Form 990 [2374](#cite:2374).
for_grant_seekers: A medical research organisation conducts research itself and is a public charity; it states its status on Schedule A of Form 990 and does not file [Form 990-PF](#term:form-990-pf) [2374](#cite:2374) [2238](#cite:2238).

name: Foundation created by Congress beside a federal agency
what: Congress has set up non-profit foundations that sit beside a federal agency and raise private money for its mission [2448](#cite:2448) [2449](#cite:2449). The Foundation for the [National Institutes of Health](#term:nih) was established by Congress in 1990 [2448](#cite:2448). The [CDC](#term:cdc) Foundation describes itself as an independent non-profit created by Congress [2449](#cite:2449). The National Fish and Wildlife Foundation was created by Congress in 1984 [2452](#cite:2452). The National Park Foundation was chartered by Congress in 1967 [2455](#cite:2455).
who_qualifies: Each is named in its own statute; the federal [forecast](#term:forecast) for the CDC Foundation's administrative award cites section 399G of the Public Health Service Act, 42 U.S.C. 280e-11 [2451](#cite:2451).
how_decided: By act of Congress; each describes itself as a [501(c)(3) organisation](#term:section-501c3) [2448](#cite:2448) [2449](#cite:2449) [2452](#cite:2452).
for_grant_seekers: They differ in whether an outsider can apply [2453](#cite:2453) [2450](#cite:2450). The National Fish and Wildlife Foundation awards funding on a competitive basis through posted [requests for proposals](#term:open-call) [2453](#cite:2453). The CDC Foundation sub-grants project money through requests for proposals and states "we do not accept or respond to [unsolicited proposals](#term:unsolicited-request)" [2450](#cite:2450). The pages read for the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health and the National Park Foundation describe no [grant](#term:grant) programme open to outside applicants [2448](#cite:2448) [2455](#cite:2455).

name: Federated fund (United Way and similar)
what: A federated fund is a joint fundraising effort, usually run by a non-profit umbrella organisation, that distributes the money to several non-profits [2408](#cite:2408). United Way is the largest network of this kind named in this sweep: it counts 1,100+ United Ways in more than 30 countries and territories [2456](#cite:2456).
who_qualifies: Local United Ways are distinct non-profit organisations that develop their own priorities and programmes [2457](#cite:2457).
how_decided: Each local United Way decides its own funding; United Way Worldwide says most programme funding happens locally [2457](#cite:2457).
for_grant_seekers: A non-profit seeking United Way money goes to its local United Way, found through the locator by state or zip code, and follows that organisation's own process [2457](#cite:2457) [2456](#cite:2456).

name: Giving circle
what: A giving circle is a group of people who pool gifts and decide together where the money goes [2458](#cite:2458). Philanthropy Together, a network for such groups, describes collective giving as groups that "decide together where to give their money, time, and talents" [2458](#cite:2458).
who_qualifies: No IRS page read in this sweep defines a giving circle; the description is the network's own [2458](#cite:2458).
how_decided: By each circle's members [2458](#cite:2458).
for_grant_seekers: Philanthropy Together publishes a directory of circles; whether a circle takes applications is for each circle to say, and the page read does not state a general practice [2458](#cite:2458).
